texts.preamble: Venkatesh vs Thimmegowda on 1 July, 2025 Kabc020051202023 Before The Court Of 10th Additional Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At: Bengaluru (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc No.1020/2023
texts.facts: 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 10-11-2022 at about 7:00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L-5476 as a pillion rider, on Tumkur-Bengaluru NH-48 road. The said motorcycle was ridden by one Chethan in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing the traffic rules and regulations. While so proceeding, at Kuluvanahalli 'U' turn, they were crossing the road towards Lakkenahalli side. At that time, suddenly the rider of Hero Splendor Motorcycle Venkatesh vs Thimmegowda on 1 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100673821/ 2 bearing Engine No.JA07ABM9B00645, Chassis No.MBLJAW187M9B00660, came from Tumkur towards Bengaluru side, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing the traffic rules and regulations and both the vehicles colluded with each other. Consequently, the petitioner, riders and the pillion rider of both the vehicles fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to V.P. Magnus Hospital, Binnamangala Village, Nelamangala Taluk, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient. Earlier to the accident, he was working as agriculturist and was earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month. But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity. The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the riders of both the motorcycles bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L-5476 and Engine No.JA07ABM9B00645, Chassis No. MBLJAW187M9B00660, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L-5476. Likewise, the respondent No.3 is the owner and respondent No.4 i s t h e i n s u r e r o f t h e H e r o S p l e n d o r m o t o r c y c l e b e a r i n g E n g i n e No.JA07ABM9B00645, Chassis No.MBLJAW187M9B00660. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.2 to 4 have appeared through their counsel. The respondents No.2 and 4 have filed their separate written statements. The respondent No.3 did not choose to file his written statement. Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent. Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte. 4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L-5476 and its validity as on the date of accident. Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by him. It has contended that, in the alleged accident there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L-5476, the rider of the said motorcycle drove the same in very slow manner, in extreme left side of the road by following all traffic rules and regulations. At that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Engine No.JA07ABM9B00645, Chassis No. MBLJAW187M9B00660 rode the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L-5476. Hence, the present petition is not maintainable against this respondent and liable to be dismissed. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 5. Whereas, the respondent No.4 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.3 in respect of motorcycle bearing Engine No.JA07ABM9B00645, Chassis No.MBLJAW187M9B00660 and its validity as on the date of accident.
texts.arguments: Further it is contended that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L-5476 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to ride the same as on the date of accident, which is in contravention of the policy conditions and the Motor Vehicles Act. The owner of the said vehicle has allowed the rider to rode the same knowing fully well that, he has no valid and effective driving licence, thereby there is clear violation of the policy terms and conditions and the Motor Vehicles Act. Further it is contended that, at the time of alleged accident, the petitioner was not wearing safety head gear, the medical bills claimed by the petitioner are not paid Venkatesh vs Thimmegowda on 1 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100673821/ 3 by him and are not supported with the proper receipts and they are created for the purpose of duplicate claim. The claim petition is not filed well within time and is barred by limitation. As such the present claim petition is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed. It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act. Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. It has contended that, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-52-L-5476 was rash and negligent in his riding and responsible for the alleged accident and for which self negligence of the petitioner has contributed. Further it is contended that, the rider of the insured motorcycle bearing Engine No.JA07ABM9B00645, Chassis No.MBLJAW187M9B00660 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident, which is in contravention of the policy conditions and the Motor Vehicles Act. The owner of the said vehicle has allowed the rider to ride the same, knowing that he has no valid and effective driving licence, thereby there is clear violation of the policy terms and conditions and the Motor Vehicles Act. Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.3, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses incurred and treatment taken by him. It has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied." The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc. The learned counsel for respondent No.4 vehemently argued that, the Ex.P.6 charge-sheet clearly speaks that, as on the date of accident the accused/rider of the offending Hero Splendor Motorcycle bearing Engine No.JA07ABM9B00645, Chassis No.MBLJAW187M9B00660 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and hence in addition to the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of I.P.C., he has been charge-sheeted for offence punishable U/Sec.181, 192(1) of Motor Vehicles Act. In such circumstances, the respondent No.3/owner of offending vehicle, who has consciously handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid driving licence, cannot be permitted to take the benefit of his wrong and the respondent No.4/Insurance Company is entitled to raise a defence under Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act. On the other hand, the learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that, it is settled principle of law that, the insurance company is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured, even if there is a breach of fundamental condition, recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor vehicles Act. 24.
